note: Only claims checked against a source. coordStatus 'unplaced' means no verified coordinates exist; the astronaut pins the target on the map.

targets.name: Bradbury Landing (reference base)
targets.summary: Curiosity's landing site (6 Aug 2012). Used as the start point of the simulated EVA.
targets.why: A published location and elevation give a fixed anchor for distance calculations.
targets.limits: Reference point only. The boxwork lies higher up Mount Sharp.

targets.name: Gale Crater (approx. centre)
targets.summary: Gale Crater is about 154 km across. Mount Sharp, about 5 km tall, rises from its centre.
targets.limits: Centre position is approximate. The 154 km width is not confirmed by a source ARES has checked.

targets.name: Boxwork ridge
targets.summary: Boxwork ridges stand roughly 1 to 2 m tall, crisscross the surface for miles, and have sandy hollows between them. Curiosity confirmed that dark lines along the ridges are fractures.
targets.why: Scientists propose groundwater flowed through fractures and left minerals that hardened the ridges, while wind removed the softer rock between. A drilled ridge sample contained clay minerals.
targets.limits: Ridges can be not much wider than Curiosity itself. How this applies to an astronaut on foot is not established.

targets.name: Sandy hollow between ridges
targets.summary: Sandy depressions between ridges. A drilled bedrock sample from a hollow contained carbonate minerals.
targets.why: Comparing clay in the ridge with carbonate in the hollow helps test how groundwater shaped each.
targets.limits: JPL engineers warned of wheel slip and turning trouble in the sand of hollows. This is a rover observation, not established for an astronaut.

targets.name: Nodule field
targets.summary: Pea-sized bumpy nodules imaged by Curiosity's MAHLI camera on 21 Aug 2025 (sol 4636), a 50-image mosaic, PIA26697. They were found along ridge walls and in hollows, not near the central fractures.
targets.why: Nodules formed from minerals left as groundwater dried out. Scientists say they cannot yet fully explain why the nodules sit where they do.
targets.limits: The sources we have do not give the map location of this image.
